answer: In an agent market trading cedar, voting power follows deposited collateral, not account count: each token grants one vote and stays locked for 90 days, even if its owner creates more agents. A tide of fake identities therefore cannot multiply influence; each account can only echo the voting weight assigned to its share of the deposit. To gain control, an attacker must acquire and immobilize a majority of the staked tokens, bearing the capital cost and price risk.
